in: I can't wait to see you exclamation point Let's meet at seven period
expect_rules: I can't wait to see you! Let's meet at seven.
note: Wispr's verbatim R1 example [DOC]. The glyphs are rules-owned; `seven` -> `7` is R6 and is covered by a17.

in: are we still on for lunch question mark
expect_rules: are we still on for lunch?
note: Terminal mark by name in a messaging surface.

in: the file is called notes underscore final
expect_rules: the file is called notes_final
note: A tight glyph binds both neighbours with no spaces.

in: she said quotation mark ship it quotation mark and then left
expect_rules: she said "ship it" and then left
note: The quote name alternates open -> close so a pair wraps the words between.

in: the plan em dash ship it tomorrow
expect_rules: the plan—ship it tomorrow
note: Em dash is tight; the hyphenated spelling normalises to the same name.

in: add a dash of salt to the pot
expect_rules: add a dash of salt to the pot
note: A determiner in front of a mark name makes it the noun the speaker means.

in: When is reading club new line should be tomorrow
expect_rules:
When is reading club
should be tomorrow
note: Wispr's verbatim R2 example [DOC]. R2 owns the break, and that half is asserted exactly; the `?` and the re-cased second line are R4/LLM work and are not in the golden.

in: the draft is done new paragraph I will send it tonight
expect_rules:
the draft is done

I will send it tonight
note: `new paragraph` / `skip a line` / `start a new paragraph` all widen to a blank line.

in: here is the summary skip a line the numbers are attached
expect_rules:
here is the summary

the numbers are attached
note: Alternate spoken form of the paragraph break.

in: let new line equal period separated tokens
expect_rules: let new line equal period separated tokens
note: Code mode never reaches the mark pass or the list renderer: dictated identifiers are returned verbatim.

in: sounds good to me.
expect_rules: sounds good to me.
note: R3 [DOC]: a short chat dictation drops its final period. Not implemented in the rules stage yet (spec item YV59) - the golden records what the pipeline does today.

in: sounds good to me.
expect_rules: sounds good to me.
note: R3's negative half [DOC]: outside messaging surfaces the period stays and the line is capitalised.

in: the build is green and the tests all pass
expect_rules: the build is green and the tests all pass
note: R4: a non-chat dictation that ends bare gets a period.

in: can you review this before standup
expect_rules: can you review this before standup
note: R4: an interrogative opener takes `?` rather than `.`.

context: I went to the store and
in: They were out of milk
expect_rules: they were out of milk
note: R5: mid-sentence caret lowercases the lead word. Applied by `join_with_context` after cleanup, exactly as lib.rs wires it.

in: the tests all pass
expect_rules: The tests all pass
note: R5: a fresh sentence at the caret capitalises the lead word and needs no extra space.

in: let's meet at seven
expect_rules: let's meet at seven
note: R6 [DOC]: `at seven` -> `at 7`. Digit normalisation is not implemented yet; the golden is today's behaviour.

in: const seven = seven + one
expect_rules: const seven = seven + one
note: R6's hard guard: numerals inside code are left exactly as dictated.

in: let's meet Tuesday, wait no, Friday
expect_rules: let's meet Friday
note: Measured failure #5 [REP]. The retracted weekday is dropped on purpose, so it is declared - everything else must survive.

in: um so like the thing is we should probably ship it
expect_rules: so like the thing is we should probably ship it
note: Measured failure #6. The leading `um` goes; the un-bounded `like` does NOT - YV58 removes a hedge only where it is a discourse particle (comma-bounded or sentence-initial), and this one is neither. The capital and the period are R4/LLM. All three gaps are still open, so the golden records them.

in: I wanted to buy a record as a gift, as a present.
expect_rules: I wanted to buy a record as a gift, as a present.
note: Measured failure #4 [DOC]. Restatement is not rule-expressible - the rules stage leaves it and the LLM owns the fix.

in: let's do coffee at 2 actually 3
expect_rules: let's do coffee at 3
note: The documented `actually` restatement [DOC], same-category (a number replaces a number).

in: I actually enjoyed the movie
expect_rules: I actually enjoyed the movie
note: [DOC] negative case: `actually` as an adverb is content, never a retraction marker.
